review: Complete three implementation and three test files read. Existing first-party source plus explicit synthetic authorization/provider fixtures. No real tokens, session records, identities or private history exported.

Account binding readiness displays sanitized provider/HTTPS issuer/status/digested tenant references only, re-reads service state after callbacks, and keeps account linking separate from exact-task pairing.

Hung status and authorization-start requests are bounded. Stop-waiting releases UI without claiming submitted authorization was canceled. Browser sign-in removes a stale callback marker only after a new browser open succeeds; desktop success is not inferred from a URL marker.

Managed website connection recovers stalled start/check via local inspect without replaying a claim. Paid test controls retain explicit input and separate account/allowance checks; no live provider or payment action was invoked during this review.

Review found private-text and connection-status callbacks could cross account changes or unmount. Canonical UI now invalidates those callbacks and clears account-local prompts/status. Four regression cases failed before repair; all eighteen connection tests pass after. No submitted provider operation is canceled or automatically retried.
ManagedWebsiteConnection and its test are newer than R379. Remaining selected bytes are exact current canonical inputs; line-ending normalization only.
limits: Unpublished source proposal; no commit, push, new EXE or deployment.
Mock/native-bridge tests do not prove Auth0 sign-in, installed acceptance, funding settlement or service-side authorization.
Public backend, native bridge, shared schema and library dependencies are separate inputs.
UI cancellation is not provider cancellation and does not change pairing, room, game or payer grants.
